reapack.name: ReaSock.ext
reapack.desc: ReaSock: connect REAPER to other programs

version.author: Tech Audio
version.changelog: - First release: a WebSocket and ReaScript bridge between REAPER and other programs, with actions clients can register (Lend), state-change events (Tell), queries for tracks, items, takes, and markers (Ask), and a bundled API reference.

version.author: Tech Audio
version.changelog: - Security: refuse WebSocket connections from web pages unless their origin is listed in `allowedOrigins` in `~/.reasock/config.json`. Browsers don't apply cross-origin rules to WebSockets, so in 0.1.0 any website open while REAPER was running could connect to ReaSock and run REAPER actions. Native clients (Node, Python, Electron main processes) are unaffected.

version.author: Tech Audio
version.changelog: - Security: WebSocket clients must send the `token` from REAPER's instance file (`~/.reasock/instances/<pid>.json`) in `initialize` (protocol 0.3.0). The token is random each time REAPER starts, and on macOS and Linux the instance file and its folders are now readable only by your user, so other users on the machine and web pages can't connect. Scripts inside REAPER need no token. - Examples: Python (a hotkey to copy selected items' file paths, a selection follower), an MCP server for AI agents, shell helpers with websocat, a browser dashboard, and a ReaImGui inspector panel, which also ships in the ReaPack package. - `@techaudio/reasock` on npm: a typed TypeScript client (every method, param, result, and event typed from the OpenRPC description), with reconnect that restores actions and subscriptions after REAPER restarts, and a browser build.

version.author: Tech Audio
version.changelog: - `@techaudio/reasock`: a refused `connect()` (a wrong token, say) closes its connection, so a Node script exits instead of hanging. And an action or subscription REAPER refused is no longer retried on every reconnect, where it failed each time and stopped the client from ever reconnecting.

version.author: Tech Audio
version.changelog: - Added editable response curves for every mapping: click 'Edit curve' on a mapping, then right-click the pad to add a point, drag points with the right button, and Alt + right-click to remove one (endpoints stay pinned to the pad edges; drag them vertically to set the output range) - Added per-mapping curve controls in the Mappings window: use/bypass the curve, visibility (segments and/or points), color, line thickness and point radius - Added a per-project option controlling whether Y-axis curves are transposed for editing - Retired the Min/Max sliders: existing projects migrate their bounds into the curve automatically, so mappings sound exactly the same and the range is now visible and editable as the curve itself - Fixed the pad responding to clicks aimed at overlapping windows (e.g. dragging a slider in the Mappings window no longer moves mapped parameters) - Fixed mappings breaking permanently when their track was deleted mid-session; deleting a track and undoing now recovers the mapping automatically

version.author: Tech Audio
version.changelog: - Reorganized the Mappings window into a tree grouped by track, FX and parameter, with each mapping's controls laid out in resizable columns - Added axis reassignment: switch a mapping between the X and Y axes in place, keeping its curve and settings - Replaced selection-based removal with a per-mapping Remove button - Compacted the curve controls: color is now a single swatch that opens the full picker, and thickness and point radius are stepper inputs - The Mappings window now refreshes automatically when the project changes (tracks or FX added, removed or renamed) and no longer restores a stale saved window size
